claims.statement: For every finite simple graph G on m vertices, every W containing all isolated vertices of G, and every integer k>=2 with m<=2k+1, if q_j counts independent j-sets meeting W, then q_(k+1)<=q_k.
claims.scope: Arbitrary finite simple graphs; W contains all isolates; integer k>=2 and m<=2k+1. No tree, bipartite, favorable-selector, or first-descent hypothesis.
claims.reason: The addability incidence identity reduces the claim to B+C>=q_k at m=2k+1. Good sets contribute to B; bad all-isolate sets inject, by adjoining a fixed non-isolate, into multiply marked upper sets counted by C. The edgeless case is equality by complementation.

limitations: This is an informal proof audit; no Lean formalization or kernel receipt is provided.
No conclusion is transferred to leaf-specific order bands or the lower-region favorable-leaf aggregate.
